title: Industry angle summaries — fintech / healthcare / legal / gov
body:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures concise positioning angles and quick competitive notes for five priority verticals we want to prioritize in the next two quarters: fintech, healthcare, legal, enterprise SaaS (platform buyers), and government/defense. It is intentionally tactical — one page per vertical style — intended for SDRs, solutions engineers, and PMs who need short, repeatable language plus suggested proof points and quick experiments to test.

How to use this doc:
- Read the one-paragraph framing for each vertical, then the 3–4 messaging pillars, the short competitor map, and 3 rapid GTM experiments.
- Keep messaging lean; aim for <30 second value statements in outreach.
- Capture feedback from pilots in the linked Jira and update the Proof Points section.

1) Fintech (payments, neobanks, trading infra)
Framing:
Fintech teams need inference that is both ultra-low-latency and provably cost-efficient. Typical workloads: realtime conversational assistants (KYC flows, customer support), transaction monitoring (fast reranking/scoring), and portfolio-level batch inference (embeddings for similarity/alerts). Selling angle centers on predictable cost, latency SLOs, and deterministic fallbacks during peak spikes.
Core messaging pillars:
- Latency as an SLA: "Predictable sub-100ms tail latency for conversational and scoring endpoints, even under spikes."
- Cost transparency and plugging into unit economics: "Token-level cost breakdowns + batching suggestions to cut inference spend 2–4x vs naive endpoints."
- Failure modes and compliance: "Graceful fallback policies and private deployment options for sensitive datasets."
- Integration: "Out-of-the-box connectors for event-driven pipelines and low-friction SDKs for real-time productization."
Competitor snapshot:
- Cloud managed endpoints: easy but opaque latency/cost tradeoffs, usually more expensive at scale.
- Self-hosted inference vendors: cost control but hard to operationalize and maintain SLOs.
Quick GTM experiments:
- SDR email sequence that opens with: "Cut inference spend on fraud scoring by 30% without changing model" and links to a one-page cost calculator.
- Partner pilot with an observability vendor to show joint token-level traces for a shared customer.
- Send targeted content to fintech developer forums highlighting a low-latency benchmark vs 2 major cloud endpoints.
Proof points to collect:
- Benchmark showing 99th percentile latency for a 2k-context model under production traffic profile.
- Case notes from dedicated capacity pilot showing N% cost reduction or throughput improvements.

2) Healthcare (digital therapeutics, clinical decision support, patient intake)
Framing:
Healthcare buyers prioritize data privacy, auditability, and validated quality over purely chasing lowest latency. Many customers need private deployment (VPC or on-prem), KMS integration, and long retention of audit logs for regulatory review. Demonstrating processes for model validation and recordability is essential.
Core messaging pillars:
- Data sovereignty + auditability: "Private control plane with HSM/KMS integration and immutable audit logs for inference requests."
- Model validation and QA: "Eval pipelines, canary datasets and automated regression alerts tied to clinical prompts."
- Controlled degradation: "Canary rollouts + automatic fallback to a validated baseline model if regressions detected."
- Compliance partnerships: "Artifacts and templates to accelerate HIPAA / ISO readiness for inference endpoints."
Competitor snapshot:
- Large cloud vendors advertise compliance but often lack turnkey private deployments that integrate with hospital networks.
- Niche vendors offer on-prem but are not developer-friendly and require long integration cycles.
Quick GTM experiments:
- Build a short checklist + whitepaper: "Checklist for evaluating LLM inference vendors for clinical use" and promote through healthcare AI newsletters.
- Run a 6-week technical validation with a digital health startup to capture an audit log and validation report to use as a template.
- Host a webinar with a compliance partner addressing operational controls for inference.
Proof points to collect:
- Template audit log and a redacted incident runbook from a pilot.
- A successful private deployment checklist and time-to-first-inference metric (days).

3) Legal (law firms, e-discovery, contract review platforms)
Framing:
Legal teams need strong provenance, deterministic outputs for workflows, and defensible record keeping. Use cases include contract summarization, clause extraction, and assisted drafting — all of which require versioned models and strict chain-of-custody for data.
Core messaging pillars:
- Deterministic rollouts and model pinning: "Pin model versions per client and keep historic outputs for audits."
- Chain-of-custody: "Immutable request/response logs, user-attribution, and exportable audit trails."
- Cost predictability for bulk e-discovery jobs: "Reserved capacity + batch pricing for sustained high-throughput jobs."
- Integration into legal workflow tools via simple webhooks and batch APIs.
Competitor snapshot:
- Lawyer-facing SaaS often bolt on 3rd-party LLM APIs — lacks provider-level controls.
- Specialty legal inference vendors are strong on document workflows but weaker on scale and latency.
Quick GTM experiments:
- Outreach to 3 mid-market e-discovery vendors proposing a reserved capacity trial for a 30-day high-volume review.
- Co-create a sample audit export (redacted) and playbook for compliance officers.
- Publish a short memo: "How to prove model behavior in court — practical controls for inference."
Proof points to collect:
- Redacted audit artifact used in a sales conversation.
- Performance numbers for a batch contract extraction job on dedicated capacity.

4) Enterprise SaaS platform (marketplaces, CRMs, analytics platforms)
Framing:
Platform buyers prioritize developer productivity, predictable multi-tenant isolation, and cost-effective embedding/indexing/semantic search capabilities. They also care about plug-and-play observability and per-tenant quotas/permissions.
Core messaging pillars:
- Multi-tenant controls: "Per-tenant model pinning, quotas, and preemptible burst capacity."
- Developer ergonomics: "SDKs, templates, and end-to-end example integrations for several popular SaaS platforms."
- Observability + cost attribution: "Token-level billing and per-route latency/cost dashboards for engineering and finance."
- Monetization support: "Help packaging inference as a billable feature with suggested pricing bands and usage tiers."
Competitor snapshot:
- Generic API vendors have good ergonomics but limited multi-tenant billing/attribution.
- Enterprise PaaS vendors can offer infrastructure but lack inference-specific developer patterns.
Quick GTM experiments:
- Product-led growth kit: a repo with 3 starter apps (marketplace search, smart summaries in CRM, analytics narrative) for quick adoption.
- Web-based ROI calculator oriented to platform economics (upload your MAU / calls to infer ROI).
- Joint case study with a mid-market SaaS showing time-to-launch for an inference feature.
Proof points to collect:
- Template integration code and time-to-first-inference for a platform partner.
- Example dashboard screenshots with per-route cost breakdowns.

5) Government & Defense (civil agencies, defense research labs)
Framing:
Buyers care about air-gapped deployment options, FIPS/HSM integrations, and long-term support contracts. Procurement cycles are long; early wins come from compliance proofs and tactical proofs-of-concept with strong security posture.
Core messaging pillars:
- Hardened private deployments: "On-prem or VPC-private control plane, FIPS-capable crypto and HSM/KMS support."
- Long term support + SLAs: "Tiered SLAs, security patching cadence, and SOC2 / FedRAMP readiness roadmap."
- Controlled model provenance: "Signed model binaries, version manifests, and exportable attestation reports."
- Interoperability with classified networks: "Options for offline packaging and deterministic rollout scripts."
Competitor snapshot:
- Defense contractors can deliver air-gapped stacks but are costly and slow to iterate.
- Cloud vendors provide compliant environments but procurement/bureaucracy remain blockers.
Quick GTM experiments:
- Produce a short security whitepaper tailored to civil agencies describing the private control plane architecture.
- Run a workshop with one lab to demonstrate an offline packaging + attestation flow.
- Prepare a procurement-friendly SOW template to shorten legal negotiations.
Proof points to collect:
- A red team summary from a pilot and remediation timeline.
- An exemplar SOW that closed within procurement timelines.

Risks and common objections (cross-vertical)
- "We can build this ourselves": counter with total cost of ownership + time-to-market math and show reference deployments.
- "Vendor lock-in": offer model portability and exportable manifests; document rollback stories.
- "Quality regressions on updates": show canary/rollback tooling, regression alerts tied to evaluation suites.

One-sentence positioning templates (use in outreach)
- Fintech: "Redwood gives fintechs production-grade LLM inference with predictable latency and unit economics so you can ship real-time scoring and conversational features without surprises."
- Healthcare: "Run LLM inference under your control — private planes, auditable logs and validation tooling for clinical-grade workflows."
- Legal: "Defensible, auditable inference with model pinning and exportable chains-of-custody for sensitive legal workflows."
- Enterprise SaaS: "Turn inference into a billable, observable feature for your platform with multi-tenant controls and developer templates."
- Gov/Defense: "Air-gapped, audited, and SLA-backed inference deployments designed for high-assurance government programs."

Next steps and immediate output to create:
- Create 1-pager collateral per vertical + one benchmark deck (three slides) for latency/cost vs 2 major cloud endpoints.
- Draft SDR/email sequences using the one-sentence templates; run A/B test on messaging.
- Schedule pilots: 3 fintech, 2 healthcare, 1 gov engagement in the next quarter.
- Sync with product on required proof-point instrumentation: per-route cost export, signed model manifests, and an example private-deploy playbook.

Feedback log (for collab updates):
- 2024-12-01 Priya: add more specifics on HIPAA artifacts.
- 2024-12-10 Daniel: include example SOW for gov pilots.
- 2024-12-18 Ethan: request that benchmark scripts be reproducible and open-sourced.

End.
